bugs.name: Reopening an issue removes its close event without recording a reopen event
bugs.summary: Reopening an issue sets its status to Open but removes the previously displayed close event and adds no reopen event to the activity timeline, including after refresh; this repeated on a second close/reopen cycle.
bugs.expected: After reopening, the issue should be Open and its activity timeline should retain the close event and show the reopen event.
bugs.actual: The timeline showed “momentic-admin closed this issue now” while the issue was Closed. After reopening and refreshing, the status was Open, but the timeline showed only the original issue entry—neither the close event nor a reopen event remained. Repeating the close/reopen/refresh cycle produced the same result.
reproSteps: Starting at /, use the provided authenticated session as repository owner momentic-admin; no credentials were manually entered.
Create a new private repository named mo-issues-reopen-timeline-7k4p.
In that repository, create an open issue titled mo-issues-reopen-timeline-check and open its issue page at /momentic-admin/mo-issues-reopen-timeline-7k4p/issues/1.
Select Close issue and verify the Closed status and the visible “momentic-admin closed this issue now” timeline event.
Select Reopen, then refresh the issue page. Verify that the status is Open and inspect the timeline: the close event is gone and no reopen event appears.
Repeat the close, reopen, and refresh sequence once. The close event again appears while Closed and both status-transition events are absent after reopening.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected the reported expectation as inconsistent with intended behavior. This is an explicit noise-reduction feature, not lost database history. The introducing release note says contradictory timeline actions are canceled and not displayed. The pinned TestCombineOpenClose contains close_open_nullified, with a close followed ten seconds later by reopen and afterCombined=nil. Its next case preserves both comments when reopen occurs after sixty-one seconds. Issue and pull-request conversations share this aggregator. The candidate expects every visible close/reopen event to remain; that expectation directly conflicts with the documented and tested aggregation contract for nearby uninterrupted changes by the same author. This issue report has the same tested rapid close/reopen nullification as the pull-request report.
